name: HuBERT-EE: Early Exiting HuBERT for Efficient Speech Recognition
problem: Self-supervised encoders are deep enough that a large share of utterances finish long before the last layer, and the remaining layers are wasted compute.
mechanism: Attaches multiple early-exit branches at intermediate layers. Each branch emits a prediction and a confidence score; when the score passes a threshold the forward pass STOPS and that result is returned, so cost becomes data-dependent rather than fixed.
speedup_reported: Reports acceleration of HuBERT inference on LibriSpeech while balancing the accuracy/latency tradeoff. The paper does not quote a single speedup factor in the abstract, so no number is recorded here - the mechanism (per-utterance dynamic depth) is the transferable part.
notes:
Interspeech 2024 per the arXiv comment. Early exiting is attractive for a batch-1 serving path because it makes mean latency data-dependent, but it is hostile to batched GPU serving: divergent exit depths force padding to the deepest member of the batch, which erases the saving exactly when the GPU is best utilised. Recorded as research-only for that reason - it is a CPU/latency-bound win, not a throughput win.
